items.text: the agency inbox now has a search box and a Group-by funnel, with collapsible per-supplier cards and rollup banners so a project's conversations read at a glance. An Unread filter surfaces only the threads needing action, each row shows " · N items", and opening a thread brings up the full conversation in a dialog with a details panel. Project links use readable references.
the Reports tab is back on an active project, with the Ballpark and Statement-of-Work document creators.

fixes.text: rebuild-env table gaps — brand config and coachmarks tables were missing on the isolated environments, so those surfaces failed to save; both added.
inbox accessibility and the supplier search count — screen-reader labelling and the per-supplier "
inbox supplier-engagement guard — a supplier can only open a thread for a project it is actually engaged on.

items.text: select several items at once — in card, list or table view — and act on them in one pass: make active / inactive, submit for approval, approve / reject (admins), reclassify into another category, delete, or refresh their images. Available to suppliers on their own shop and to Ballpark admins across shops, with each action gated to who may perform it.
filter a shop by whether an item has a photo (Any / Yes / No), and re-pull images for the ones missing them straight from the source listing — fixing imageless items without a full re-import.

move an item (or a whole selection) into a different category from one dialog that opens on the item's current home; the category rail refreshes on the spot — no page reload — when items are reclassified or added.

analysing a supplier's website now persists, so you can start it, step away, and come back to the results rather than re-running it. Image pulls prioritise a listing's own product photos within the fetch budget.

each marketplace filter now carries a label above it — Price / Tier / Status / Active / Images — in the same style as an editable form field, with plain Any / Yes / No choices where it fits; the filter control and the single-supplier store header were tidied to match.
every page header now shares a single hero style (the home greeting face), so the title and its label read identically across Home, Projects, Marketplace, Profile and My Shop.

a Ballpark admin can no longer edit another organisation's items simply by being an admin. Admin reach is now read-only except for two narrow, column-scoped actions enforced at the database itself: moderation (approve / reject and soft-delete) and the image refresh (images only). Hardened by an end-of-arc security and Angular audit this cycle.

Ballpark rebuilt on a streamlined data model and promoted to its first fully-isolated preview environment: its own database, backend and frontend, with no shared infrastructure. Tenant isolation is enforced at the database itself (row-level security + a non-owner application role + per-request identity), hardened this cycle by a security audit — quote ownership pinned at the database, message parties made immutable, and supplier quote edits restricted to soft-delete.

a project now has two views: a draft Ballpark quote (scope + indicative costs) and an active Running budget. The budget shows supplier-first cards grouped by supplier — a per-supplier status pill, item rows (item · quantity · quick view · status · cost · subtotal), and payment tiles (paid · outstanding · final 50%) once a line is agreed — with a Draft ⇄ Active selector, a Details tab, and your own costs alongside.

agency ↔ supplier negotiation is tracked as a journal of events; each line's status reads "To agree" through "All confirmed", shown consistently in both the inbox and the Running budget from one shared source.
a running-ballpark pill shows the live total and item count; a chevron collapses the hero cover while the detail bar keeps the key stats and the project name.

the marketplace tab now scrolls at the window edge like the other tabs; Type (Items / Suppliers), filter and cart controls sit on one line above a full-width search, with the category rail aligned to the first row of cards.
a single-row app header (logo · navigation · account + Sign Out, pinned to the window edges); "Past projects" is now simply Projects throughout.
the status-pill wording is now editable in Settings ▸ Codelists (`line_display_status`), with the line, provider and quote status lists seeded.
Add an image per variant value in the editor (one photo per option, e.g. the orange chair for Colour: Orange).

The item dialog cover is now a carousel — arrows page through the item photo and each option's image, and picking an option switches the cover to that option's image (nothing changes if the option has no image). The photo gallery is unchanged.

Item variants — suppliers configure choices as variant dimensions (e.g. Size, Paper Type, Colour); each value is priced as No cost, an Upcharge (+£), or an absolute Cost. Edited inline in the item editor.
Options folded into variants — one consistent model, including free "pick one" choices like colour. The old separate Options list is retired.
Tags & Tier are now editable in an item's Classification, with a one-click "What's Hot" tag (Tier gains Bronze / Silver / Gold).
Item descriptions keep their formatting (bold, bullet lists) from the supplier's own site.
What's Hot — a store's shopfront leads with its What's Hot items and surfaces a What's Hot menu link when it has any.
Variant products show a configurator — pick the options, see the price update, with the cost shown on hover — and require a choice before adding to a ballpark.
Supplier cards and the project Suppliers tab polish carried over from v0.3.x.
The chosen variant carries into the quote — the option ("Ivory · Bedazzled") shows on the line, the cart, the preview panel and the client quote document.
A variant's upcharge prices per unit on top of any volume tier (e.g. £2.99 + £0.50 = £3.49 each).
Set the quantity directly in the item dialog.
The item dialog's close button now fully closes the preview.
Per-unit prices show pence where present, so unit × quantity reconciles with the line total.

supplier tiles now render consistently across the grid: a store can fill the tile with its cover photo or fit its logo on a clean white ground, set per supplier. Owners choose it on their profile (Branding), and platform admins can set it for any store — so a mix of photos, logos and logo-as-cover art all look intentional.

the quick-view "Add to ballpark" now shows the chosen variant combination's price; the project Suppliers tab browses every category ("All Categories" lists every store, not just those already in the quote); the Supplier filter is wider so long names fit; and supplier cards gain a soft rose footer.

supplier products that come in variations (size × sides × quantity, and the like) are now captured as a full priced matrix. On the shopfront the item's quick view shows a configurator: pick each option and the exact price resolves ("From £53" until every option is chosen). Also fixes an import bug where a variable product could be imported as one of its variations (wrong price, no description, no options).

a single-category shopfront now lists its subcategories on the menu; clicking a subcategory card browses its items in place; clicking any item opens the quick view (with an Edit pencil for people with edit rights) instead of jumping away; long descriptions collapse behind "Show more"; and the category menu scrolls with left/right arrows instead of a scrollbar.

the supplier page now leads with a proper brand banner: the cover image sits behind the name and the tab bar, with a full-width category menu beneath it. Browse a category or subcategory and its items appear in place under a titled header — no page change. A full-width mega-menu spans each category's subcategories, and supplier logos render reliably (including logo-only SVGs).

fixes.text: Storefront & marketplace polish — the marketplace category rail is now supplier-filter aware; the "From" price shows pence for items under £100; catalogue extraction lifts its per-run cap to 500 URLs; de-duplication keeps the deeper (subcategory) URL; the taxonomy manager no longer double-creates a category; and imported supplier text decodes HTML entities.

items.text: onboard a supplier by reading their existing website. Auto-detects the platform (WooCommerce · WordPress · generic site), reads the catalogue the optimal way — structured API where one exists, intelligent crawl otherwise — and stages every product as pending for review. Runs as a background job with live progress, cancel and re-attach; tracks AI cost per pull; and dedupes by vendor identity so re-runs only add new products, never duplicates.

a live three-level category manager: create, rename, delete, and move or reparent whole branches of the marketplace taxonomy — with no data migration. Items ride along by reference, so reshaping the tree is instant.

browse now understands the full three-level taxonomy: subcategory filters, descendant item counts, and a three-level drill-down rail. Items classified at any depth roll up to their parent so nothing is hidden.

a redesigned item editor built on canonical attribute groups (Specifications · Features · Style · Measurements · Materials) plus priced Options, with save-on-blur, cascading Category ▸ Subcategory ▸ Sub-sub classification, and delete-with-cascade.

manage organisations end-to-end: list, filter and search all orgs, create a new org, approve or suspend suppliers, and edit any org's profile — with website import to pre-fill a new supplier's brand, About and details from their existing site.
a full supplier view for admins (Profile · My Shop · Shopfront) plus the ability to add catalogue items on a supplier's behalf, routed through the same approval flow as supplier-added items.

every organisation's data is isolated at the database itself: a non-owner application role under row-level security, with org identity re-proven from a signed token on every request. A mis-scoped query cannot leak another tenant's data — the database is the backstop, not application discipline.

fixes.text: Cart shows a single "Go with this Ballpark" (removed the redundant "Edit in marketplace")
Supplier name now shown on the estimate/cart item rows
Back from the Quote / SOW document returns to Reports (where it opened); the button reads "Back"
Inbox tab now sits next to Overview in the project workspace
Messaging suppliers lands on the live Overview, with an attention badge on the Inbox tab
Supplier name now shown on the marketplace + supplier-store item cards (no longer hidden behind the city)

items.text: build a project from a brief, ballpark the cost, message suppliers, quote the client.
list products, run a shop & storefront, respond to quote requests.
curate the taxonomy, approve items, manage roles & codelists.
multi-tenant organisations: every agency and supplier is an org; members join via user_orgs with a derived effective role; all data and settings are org-scoped.
user profile & account settings: your details, preferences, and sign-in identity.

AI-first project creation from a written brief; a project workspace (Overview · Inbox · Ballpark Cost · Marketplace · Reports); cost estimate with quantities, margin, contingency, VAT & insurance; a live-project flow once suppliers are messaged.
per-supplier message threads with an inbox landing (per-supplier action rollups) and quote requests raised from a project.
parses a written brief into a structured project and suggests/matches marketplace items.
client records (company details, address) attached to projects and reusable across them.
client-facing quote document in an SOW layout (timeline, payment terms, special terms) with themed presentation.
browse by category → subcategory with dense item cards (Supplier · City) and Quick View; filters; available both globally and inside a project.
My Shop (your products) and My Shopfront (your brand page) on the shared Marketplace layout, plus a supplier home dashboard of what needs you.
catalogue items with per-unit or flat pricing, units, install cost, tier, and an image gallery.
15 macro categories with curated subcategories; browse + admin curation across the marketplace.
admin approves item imagery before it goes live; suppliers submit and resubmit; text & pricing edits don't force re-approval.
centralised reference lists (statuses, units, etc.) driving consistent, controlled dropdowns.
the tracking subsystem behind the roadmap itself: epics, requirements, enhancements, feedback and QC test cases, with EP-/F- refs, statuses, target-versions and releases.
Google sign-in; org-based roles (agent / supplier / admin) with permissions re-derived per request; identity-only sessions.
in-app guided help; contextual coachmark tips that explain features as you go; admins can tweak the copy.
